scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: An IT Department user (it_hod, 192.168.1.2) reports they
cannot reach CS Department hosts (192.168.2.0/24) -- inter-department routing
between IT and CS seems broken. They suspect router0 (which connects both
segments) dropped one of its department interfaces or a static/RIP entry. Please
confirm the inter-department fault.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported inter-department routing failure between the IT segment
(192.168.1.0/24) and the CS segment (192.168.2.0/24) does not exist in the
live lab. Every component involved in the path was verified and found healthy.

Router0, which serves as the single-hop gateway between the two departments,
has both its department-facing interfaces fully operational: eth0
(192.168.1.1/24, toward lan_it via switch0) and eth1 (192.168.2.1/24, toward
lan_cs via switch1) are both in UP/UP state with zero errors or drops. The
FRR RIPv2 daemon on router0 is correctly configured with network statements
for 192.168.1.0/24, 192.168.2.0/24, and 10.0.0.0/8, and the RIP table
confirms both subnets are advertised as connected-interface routes. The kernel
FIB on router0 shows both as directly connected (C>*) with no competing or
missing entries.

End-host configuration is equally correct: it_hod (192.168.1.2) has its
default gateway set to 192.168.1.1, and cs_hod (192.168.2.2) points to
192.168.2.1 — both pointing to router0. Pings from it_hod to all five CS
hosts (cs_hod, cs_lab1–4, addresses 192.168.2.2–.6) completed with 0% packet
loss and TTL=63, confirming a single router hop through router0 as expected.

Root cause: there is no fault — the helpdesk ticket describes a non-existent
condition. No corrective action is required on any device.
